entries.content: Done. The `StyleGuide.handle_error` method had two defects: it never consulted `Violation.is_inline_ignored()`, so `# noqa` comments (including on multiline f-strings, via the processor's noqa line mapping) had no effect and inline-ignored errors were still reported and counted — I restored the check (returning 0 when inline-ignored, honoring `--disable-noqa`) and removed the stray `quiet`-based filtering that didn't belong there (quiet is handled by formatter selection in `plugins/reporter.py` and crashed on namespaces without a `quiet` attribute). Separately, `FileChecker._handle_results` passed the raw 0-based plugin offset as the violation's column, so errors were displayed one column too far left (e.g. `t.py:1:0` instead of `t.py:1:1`); I added the `+ 1` conversion when handing results to the style guide, keeping stored results 0-based as the checker tests require. With both fixes the issue's multiline f-string plugin repro produces exactly the expected `t.py:1:1`-style output, and the full test suite went from 22 failures to 464/464 passing.
